## Opponent Reads

**Player 2**: **LAG/maniac, extreme calling station postflop AS PFA.** Opens very wide (~50% PFR). 3-bets/4-bets extremely wide — including premiums (AA). **As PFA**: Calls down with virtually anything — including calling multi-street donk-leads with just overcards. C-bets most flops, checks dry/paired boards. Turn: AIR → checks/folds (float profitable); MEDIUM HANDS → checks turn, calls river (station mode); REAL HANDS → shoves aggressively. Folds to turn raises even after double-barreling. **As NON-PFA (BB defend, etc.)**: Fit-or-fold — folds to c-bets when whiffing. Stabs turn with marginal holdings but gives up river on scary boards. **DONK-LEADS with strong made hands (especially in 3-bet pots).** **CHECK-RAISES with semi-bluffs/draws on wet boards** — barrels turn with equity, CHECK-FOLDS river when draw misses. **Key line: P2 check-raise flop → bet turn → check river = BUSTED DRAW — attack with river bet.** Calls 3-bets with pocket pairs (including JJ). **Exploit**: Flat opens IP with suited broadways/connectors. 3-bet QQ+/AKs only. Value bet extremely thin as PFA. Float flop c-bets. DO NOT bluff when P2 is calling with made hands. DO bluff when P2's line = busted draw. As 3-bet caller: c-bet when P2 checks (will fold air); FOLD to P2's donk-lead + turn aggression (strong). **P2 bleeds chips — tends to finish short-stacked. Target for value.**

**Player 3**: **Tight-aggressive, skilled — most dangerous opponent (~7% VPIP in raised pots). STICKIER THAN EXPECTED in limped/multiway pots** — completes SB wide (including QJo), then plays aggressively postflop. 3-bets from blinds vs ALL positions. **Confirmed trapper — wide check-raise range in BOTH 3-bet pots AND limped pots.** Will CHECK-RAISE ALL-IN with as little as top pair in limped pots. C-betting is SELECTIVE. Triple-barrels one-pair value. **Vs RAISED POTS with escalating pressure**: calls flop+turn then folds river to size. **Vs LIMPED/SMALL POTS: stickier AND more aggressive — check-raises with top pair, calls down light.** **Exploit**: Multi-street barrels work in raised pots. In limped pots, don't bluff into P3 — they fight back. Value bet wider in limped pots. Good steal target in blinds.

**Player 4**: **Loose-passive preflop, WILDLY UNPREDICTABLE postflop — part station, part maniac.** Calls wide preflop (3-bets with junk, limps wide). **CRITICAL: Capable of MASSIVE bluffs — confirmed shoved all-in with complete air (7-high, no draw) on paired board in limped pot.** Also bets multiway flops with marginal holdings. As LIMPER: Will bet flop AND shove turn with ZERO equity. ALSO still a calling station — calls river with bottom pair, 9-high. **Dual nature: bluffs huge AND calls down light.** PASSIVE with strong made hands — checks made straights through all streets. **3-bets are strong (JJ+/AQ+) but folds to 4-bets. 5-BET SHOVE includes JJ.** As single-raiser: C-bets flop, folds to turn raises — FLOATABLE. **Folds SB to button steals with sub-premium hands — confirmed.** **Exploit**: Value bet extremely wide (#1 value target when calling). DON'T auto-fold to P4's aggression in limped pots — can be pure air. CALL DOWN wider vs P4 aggression (especially limped pots). In raised pots as PFA, still floatable. Steal over P4's SB freely. **P4 accumulates chips through unpredictability — respect their stack but exploit their wide calling.**

**Player 5**: **Very tight nit (~7% VPIP), NOT truly sticky — folds to multi-street pressure.** Limps with pocket pairs, stabs flop with small bets. C-bets flop then shuts down without connection. **As CALLER facing aggression: will call ONE street then FOLDS to continued betting, especially with scare cards.** Donk-bets can be strong OR weak — weak ones fold to raises/turn barrels; strong ones ESCALATE. **ANY turn raise from P5 = monster.** **Exploit**: Two-barrel bluff donk-bets. Multi-street value bet gets only 1-2 streets max — size up earlier streets for value. FOLD to P5's turn raises always. Good steal target in blinds.

**Player 6**: **Station/spewy — wide limper, opener, AND cold-caller.** **As LIMPER: EXTREMELY sticky postflop — calls with bottom pair. Folds preflop to large raises/steals.** **As COLD-CALLER: Donk-leads with AIR/weak draws → RAISE for fold equity. CHECK-CALLS with real made hands — passive line = actual hand.** Key tell: P6 donk-lead = air; P6 check-call = real hand. **P6 RAISES/RE-RAISES can be SEMI-BLUFFS with combo draws.** Willing to get stacks in with draws on wet boards. MASSIVE overbets = value. **4-bet shoves are NUTTED.** **Confirmed folds BB to 3x button steals.** **Exploit**: Value bet wide. SIZE DOWN iso-raises (~3x) to keep P6 in when you have value. NEVER bluff check-calling P6. RAISE donk-leads (they're air). FOLD to 4-bet shoves/overbets. Steal over P6's BB freely with standard sizing.

**Player 7**: **CONFIRMED extremely wide opener — opens trash hands (T3o from MP).** Can go long stretches without raising then open with complete junk. DON'T assume P7 opens are strong. **Wide limper too. PREFLOP MANIAC in escalated pots** — calls 5-bets with QQ/suited junk, 6-bets with weak aces. Any Ax or pocket pair = "premium" in reraised pots. **Postflop**: Commits with made hands (two pair+) — will 3-bet flop and call off. **Exploit**: Iso-raise wide over P7's opens. Value bet relentlessly. In reraised pots, get it in with any premium. **P7 tends to bust or go very short — look to finish them off.**

## Self-Assessment & Strategic Corrections

### 1. Refine “Passive = Always Value” Heuristic
Passive players can find river bluffs in capped multiway pots, particularly when scare cards hit perceived preflop raiser range.

**Adjustment:**
- Use card removal and range interaction analysis before folding automatically.
- Distinguish between brick rivers (value-heavy) and scare rivers (higher bluff density).

### 2. Multiway Donk Interpretation
Tiny turn donks from loose-passive players frequently represent:
- Medium pairs seeking cheap showdown
- Block/protection bets

Not just weak draws.

**Adjustment:**
- Avoid overestimating fold equity versus these lines.

### 3. Short-Stack Preflop Discipline
Biggest session-level leak: too many low-quality entries/continues with dominated or weak holdings when stacks got shorter.

**Adjustment:**
- Tighten further at sub-20BB, especially with weak offsuit broadway fragments, raggy aces, weak queens, and low suited trash.
- Prefer clean shove/fold or raise/fold structures over marginal flats/defends.
- Do not let recent losses create “must play” urgency; preserve fold equity and wait for stronger classes of hands.

### 4. Avoid Results-Oriented Looseing After Early Success
A couple of successful weak-hand steals should not widen baseline ranges.

**Adjustment:**
- Separate exploitative steals from default opens.
- If table is folding a lot, expand from the top of fold region first, not from dominated trash.

### 5. Table Image for Next Session
This session likely reinforced an image of generally tight/passive preflop selection with occasional weak stabs when short.

**Adjustment:**
- Early next session, expect decent fold equity on credible opens/3-bets until shown otherwise.
- Protect that image; avoid spewy low-equity entries that reduce future steal credibility.
